**Astur v2.6.1** — Right Alt is the default Astur key, and the default letter
keys are laid out around it.

## Download

`astur-windows-x64.zip` — unzip it anywhere and run `astur.exe`. No installer, no
admin rights. The zip holds two files side by side:

- `astur.exe` — the window manager (single Rust binary)
- `astur_settings.py` — the settings editor (Python 3 with tkinter)

## What's new

### Right Alt is the default main key

`main_key = ralt` out of the box: Right Alt is reserved for Astur, Left Alt stays
the apps' Alt (menu bars, Alt+F4), and Alt+Tab still passes through unless you
switch on the Astur switcher. Left Alt is still one line away (`main_key = lalt`);
the other choices are unchanged.

On layouts where Right Alt is AltGr (German, French, …) AltGr characters — `@` is
AltGr+Q on a German layout — stop typing while Astur runs, so switch to `lalt`
there.

### A key layout for a right-handed key

The default single-key binds moved to the keys under the left hand next to the
Right Alt it is held with:

| Action | Was | Now |
|---|---|---|
| Focus next / previous window | `J` / `K` | `D` / `A` |
| Swap with next / previous | `Shift+J` / `Shift+K` | `Shift+D` / `Shift+A` |
| Shrink / grow master | `H` / `L` | `Z` / `C` |
| Promote to master | `M` | `S` |
| Centre the scrolling column | `C` | `X` |

`T` (tiling), `F` (float), `W` (close), `E` (fill the workspace), `R` (cycle
width), `[` / `]` (stack) and the scrolling heights (`Shift+Z` / `Shift+C`) keep
their keys.

### The Win+L special case is gone

Astur used to move grow-master from `L` to `O` when `main_key = win`, because
Windows always keeps Win+L. That unrequested remap silently changed a shortcut, so
it is removed: with `main_key = win`, a shortcut on `L` simply does nothing there,
and it is up to you to pick another key.

## Notes

- Your existing `%USERPROFILE%\.astur\astur.conf` is never rewritten. The new
  defaults reach new installs, and **Restore defaults** in the editor (or
  `astur_settings.py`) picks them up per section.
- Nothing else changed: same binary, same Python settings editor, same zip.
